messages:
maya: Hey team — quick sync on continuous-batching tweaks for the non-chat reranker/embeddings endpoint. I'm seeing a subtle p95 regression after the kernel-selector change; baseline (yesterday's prod) for rerank_v2: p50=18ms, p95=120ms, tokens/s=8k, cost/1k tokens=$0.32. After kernel selector landed we have p95=170ms while throughput steady. Suspect batching heuristic + KV cache churn combined with the selector defaulting to int8 kernels for short sequences. Anyone else observed this?

jia: I dug into profiler traces. For sequences <128 tokens we now pick int8 kernel by default which is 2–3x faster on long sequences but shows higher dispatch overhead for many tiny requests (kernel init + dequant path). Also KV cache shuffles more often because the batch formation now groups heterogeneous seq_lens. Patch idea: prefer fp16 kernel when avg_seq_len_in_batch < 96, and bias batch formation to group similar seq_len buckets. I have a draft: commit 9f3b2e7 (wip).

sahil: +1 on the seq_len bucket idea. I also noticed KV cache eviction metrics spike when batch sizes oscillate; we keep per-worker KV windows of 30s which is aggressive for rerank (short-lived). Lowering retention to 8s cut memory churn in staging. Link to flamegraphs: https://perf.redwood/flows/1772/rerank-flame-174

perf-bot: Latest perf-run #1772 finished: throughput delta -0.5%, p50 +1ms, p95 +42ms; CI flagged regression on rerank_v2 when kernel_selector=v2 + continuous_batcher=on. See /artifacts/1772/results.json.

anders: From a queue-policy view I think we can tighten max_wait to reduce tail. Current config: {max_wait_ms: 8, token_budget: 1024, max_batch_tokens: 4096}. Proposal for rerank non-chat: {max_wait_ms: 4, token_budget: 512, max_batch_tokens: 2048} — rationale: rerank requests have small seqs and are latency-sensitive; smaller token_budget prevents a single long request from blocking many tiny ones. We should A/B this under 10/90 and watch p95 + throughput.

maya: Sounds reasonable. I'll run an AB test on canary (10%) with that config. Quick experiment config snippet:```json
{
  "endpoint": "rerank_v2",
  "split": {"canary": 0.1, "control": 0.9},
  "canary_config": {"max_wait_ms": 4, "token_budget": 512, "batcher_mode": "length_bucket"},
  "metrics": ["p50","p95","tokens_s","kv_evictions_per_min"]
}
```I'll schedule at 00:30 UTC and will attach perf traces.

nora: Two questions — 1) does length_bucket grouping interact with kernel selection? if we group by seq_len bucket we reduce heterogeneity so int8 path might be more appropriate for some buckets — need mapping by avg_len -> kernel_hint. 2) about KV cache: are we mapping cache keys by model_variant + client_id? we need to avoid cross-variant cache pollution. Currently code uses (model_id, shard) only; we should add variant tag.

maya: Good catches. Plan of action: 1) run 10% canary with new queue policy + length_bucketer; 2) apply fp16-for-short-seqs kernel hint in canary bucket; 3) reduce KV retention to 8s for rerank workers in canary; 4) add model_variant tag to KV keys in a follow-up (will open PR). I'll post perf links and the flamegraphs after the run. Thanks 😄 :thumbsup:

(small follow-up later)

maya: Canary finished — initial numbers: canary p95=95ms (control 170ms), p50=20ms (control 18ms), throughput -1.2% (within tolerance). KV_evictions down ~60%. Opening roll request to promote to 50% if no regressions overnight.
